flags.why: The gloss incorrectly requires a tool, although vớt also covers retrieving someone or something from water by hand ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-v%E1%BB%9Bt)).
flags.fix: to fish out; to scoop out; to retrieve from water or liquid

flags.why: The entry omits the common regional verb meaning to defend someone or take their side ([regional dictionary](https://www.art2all.net/chantran/chantran_tho/tranngocbao/tudienphuongnguhue/tudienphuongnguhue_B.htm)).
flags.fix: verb [Southern, Central] | to defend someone; to take someone's side

flags.why: Dị giáo means heresy, while a heretic is a person who follows it ([Cambridge dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/vi/dictionary/english-vietnamese/heresy)).

Thanh minh means explaining to clear oneself or someone else of blame or suspicion, rather than neutrally clarifying a misunderstanding ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-thanh%20minh)).
flags.fix: to explain in order to clear oneself or someone else of blame or suspicion

flags.why: Ngự describes stately sitting or royal activities and does not itself mean to rule or govern ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-ng%E1%BB%B1)).
flags.fix: to sit enthroned; to be seated in a stately manner (of a king or deity)
